questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Samoa?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Samoa article.

questions.proof: The capital of Samoa is Apia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Samoa?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Samoa on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Samoa article.

questions.proof: They are part of the United States, but they are similar to the country Samoa, and they also speak Samoan.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Samoa?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Samoa article.

questions.proof: The languages spoken in Samoa include Samoan and English.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “A measles outbreak began in October _____ and continued through December.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Samoa article.

questions.proof: A measles outbreak began in October 2019 and continued through December.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It became independent from New Zealand in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Samoa article.

questions.proof: It became independent from New Zealand in 1962.
